Anthropic released the "Claude 4" family, consisting of two models—Claude Opus 4 and Claude Sonnet 4—on May 8, 2025 [Source: ev-1]. The launch featured distinct pricing structures to target different use cases: Opus 4 was priced at $15 per million input tokens and $75 per million output tokens as the flagship model, while Sonnet 4 was priced lower at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, positioning it as a fast workhorse and developer-default coding model [Source: ev-1].

The release signaled that agentic coding had become the defining product category of 2025, with Anthropic timing the launch to coincide with the rise of Claude Code [Source: ev-1]. By highlighting "computer use 2.0" capabilities that were roughly twice as reliable as the previous 3.x generation, Anthropic positioned itself against competitors like OpenAI’s o-series during an enterprise agentic-coding gold rush [Source: ev-1]. The strategy emphasized safety and reliability for coding agents, which contributed to record API usage and ultimately helped cement Anthropic's position as a leader in this market segment [Source: ev-1].
